key: Kalman Filtering + Metamorphic Testing + Sparse Coding

concepts.name: Kalman Filtering
concepts.short_description: Optimal recursive state estimation under noise; prediction-update cycle, Gaussian state space models.

concepts.name: Metamorphic Testing
concepts.short_description: Testing without oracle: define relations between outputs (double input, ordering unchanged). Metamorphic relations as formal mutation taxonomy.

concepts.name: Sparse Coding
concepts.short_description: Neural representations using few active neurons; energy efficiency, pattern separation, Olshausen-Field model.

hypotheses.statement: Oracle-free state estimation: a system estimates a hidden state using only relations between its own outputs on transformed inputs (metamorphic residuals as pseudo-measurements), with the hidden state represented in a sparse basis. Experiment: can MR residuals replace ground-truth measurements in a predict-update loop?

Validity of invariants is itself a sparse, drifting latent state: of many candidate relations only a few hold at any time, and which ones hold changes as the system changes. Experiment: sparse-code the violation pattern over a relation library and track it with a filter.

Self-sealing estimators: covariance collapse (filter stops listening), support lock-in (code stops switching) and trivially-passing relations are three faces of one failure, confident self-consistency while wrong. Experiment: map the region of parameter space where all three co-occur.

Change is sparse: between steps only a few code atoms switch, so innovations live in a sparse event space, and a transformation predicts which switches are lawful. Experiment: classify support flips into transform-predicted vs anomalous and use the anomalous ones as fault events.

A transformation is a time step: the pair (x, T x) can be treated as consecutive states, so the transition matrix of a filter over sparse codes is a learned representation of T, and group laws of T (T^n = I) become metamorphic relations on that matrix. Experiment: test whether learned transition matrices obey the group laws.

Sparsity rescues weak oracles: a metamorphic relation only reveals the component of a fault outside its kernel, but if faults are sparse in some basis the full fault can be reconstructed from that projection. Experiment: recover full fault vectors from MR residuals with and without a sparse prior.

A trilemma: sparse coding separates similar inputs, filtering smooths across time, metamorphic relations demand consistency across transforms; the three cannot all be maximized, and there may be a phase boundary where relation violations peak. Experiment: sweep threshold and gain and look for a ridge.

Metamorphic pseudo-measurement: the Kalman update uses the MR residual r = g(f(x)) - f(T x), whose expected value is zero under a correct model, as its measurement, estimating hidden model parameters stored as a sparse coefficient vector.

hypotheses.statement: Covariance reopening: the rate of metamorphic violations inflates process noise Q, so a filter that has become overconfident starts listening again when relations it should satisfy begin failing.

hypotheses.statement: W1 probe round 1: INSTRUMENT_FAIL. At delta=0.1 the stride disagreement statistic D gave AUC 0.493 against NIS AUC 0.490 (50 vs 50 runs); Lasso top-1 localization accuracy was 0.000 (chance 0.0625; data-free sensitivity-norm baseline 0.160); null-twin AUC 0.417. Oracle RMSE AUC 0.490; cheat success=True. Matched-model mean D 4.028 (expected 4). Outcome INSTRUMENT_FAIL by the PREREG class rules applied in code.

lenses.name: Innovation whiteness spectrum
lenses.rationale: Standard filter consistency check; the baseline every MR-based claim must beat.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: innovation sequence e_t and its covariance S_t
lenses.transformation: normalize by S_t^-1/2, compute autocorrelation and NIS
predictedSignals: mismatch shows NIS > dim and nonzero autocorrelation
failureModes: insensitive to mismatches absorbed by Q
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: baseline only; defines what MRs must add

lenses.name: Support-flip ledger
lenses.rationale: Invented: treats support changes as discrete events and asks which ones the transform predicted.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: sequence of supports S_t and transform permutation pi_T
lenses.transformation: classify each flip as lawful (predicted by pi_T(S_{t-1})) or unlawful
predictedSignals: lock-in drives flip rate to zero while true support flips
lenses.nullExpectation: lawful fraction equals that expected from random flips of equal count
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: event-level view invisible to continuous innovations

lenses.name: Oracle-debt accounting
lenses.rationale: Invented: uses hidden ground truth (visible only to the lens, never the agent) to measure how much true error the MRs can see.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: true error vector and MR residual vector
lenses.transformation: decompose true error into MR-kernel and complement components
observables: visibility ratio = complement energy / total error energy
predictedSignals: sparse prior raises recovered fraction above the visibility ratio
lenses.nullExpectation: recovered fraction equals visibility ratio (min-norm recovery)
failureModes: kernel estimate wrong if the MR is nonlinear
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: quantifies what oracle-free checking cannot see

lenses.name: Gain-threshold phase portrait
lenses.rationale: Invented for this triplicate: the two knobs that make each stage stubborn, plotted together.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: grid over steady-state gain K and threshold lambda
lenses.transformation: run tracker per cell, compute latency and MR violation rate
predictedSignals: self-sealing region with boundary on K/lambda
lenses.nullExpectation: boundary requires K and lambda independently, or no region exists
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: joint structure neither knob shows alone

lenses.name: Group-representation residue
lenses.rationale: Invented: asks whether learned code-space transitions respect the algebra of the transforms.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: learned transition matrices A_T for transforms T
lenses.transformation: compute ||A^n - I||, commutators, row concentration of |A|
predictedSignals: MR-trained dictionaries give permutation-like A with small cyclic residual
lenses.nullExpectation: shuffled-pair twin gives dense A with large residual
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: algebraic rather than predictive test of representations

lenses.name: Relational sufficiency lens
lenses.rationale: Information view of what a k-sparse bottleneck keeps.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: k-sparse retained state and MR outcomes
lenses.transformation: estimate mutual information between retained components and MR pass/fail vs reconstruction
predictedSignals: MR-selected components carry more MR information at small reconstruction cost
failureModes: MI estimation bias at small samples
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: separates what is kept for consistency from what is kept for fidelity

lenses.name: Recovery-latency ledger
lenses.rationale: Invented: measures how quickly an overconfident estimator is reopened after a regime change.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: estimate error trace around a planted change point
lenses.transformation: steps until error returns within 2 sigma; false-alarm rate before change
predictedSignals: MR-driven reopening recovers faster at equal false alarms
failureModes: change too large makes all methods equal
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: decision-level comparison at matched false-alarm budgets

experiments.hypothesis: A stride-consistency metamorphic relation detects model mismatch in a Kalman filter without ground truth, better than the NIS test, and sparse regression localizes the wrong transition entry.
experiments.mechanism: Filter with transition A' run at stride 1 and stride 2 (A'^2); disagreement normalized by its predicted covariance; Lasso of mean disagreement on per-entry sensitivity vectors.
experiments.intervention: Perturb one of 16 entries of a stable 4x4 A by delta in {0.05, 0.1, 0.2} in the filter model only.
experiments.positive_control: Oracle detector using true-state RMSE (expected AUC near 1).
experiments.observable: Mean normalized stride disagreement D per run; mean NIS per run; Lasso top-1 entry.
experiments.success_criterion: Across 50 mismatched vs 50 matched seeds at delta = 0.1: AUC(D) >= 0.80 AND AUC(D) >= AUC(NIS) + 0.05 AND Lasso top-1 localization accuracy >= 0.60 (chance 0.0625) AND null-twin AUC <= 0.60.
experiments.failure_criterion: AUC(D) < 0.70, or AUC(D) <= AUC(NIS), or localization accuracy < 0.25, or null-twin AUC > 0.60.
experiments.alternative_explanation: Stride disagreement is only a re-weighted innovation statistic and carries no information beyond NIS.
experiments.null_twin: Same runs, but the stride-2 estimate at t is compared with the stride-1 estimate at a random time t' (equal marginal variance, relation destroyed).
experiments.why_this_implementation: A linear-Gaussian toy is the smallest world where the relation's expected distribution is exactly computable; no learned component, so no ML ontology is displaced.
stupid_explanations: mismatch also inflates innovations, so any statistic detects it
normalization miscomputed so the matched model already looks mismatched
Lasso localizes by sensitivity magnitude alone regardless of data

anomalies.text: delta=0.05: oracle true-state-RMSE AUC 0.476 ~ chance; mismatch not visible between seeds even with ground truth
delta=0.1: oracle true-state-RMSE AUC 0.490 ~ chance; mismatch not visible between seeds even with ground truth
delta=0.2: oracle true-state-RMSE AUC 0.558 ~ chance; mismatch not visible between seeds even with ground truth
Lasso top-1 accuracy 0.000 below data-free sensitivity-norm baseline 0.160
matched-run Lasso top-1 concentrated on entry 13 (49/50)

experiments.hypothesis: Codes from a dictionary trained with a shift-MR consistency penalty admit a permutation-like code-space transition A for circular shift, and using A as the Kalman transition improves tracking of shifting signals.
experiments.mechanism: Learn a 64-atom dictionary on length-32 signals (sums of 3 circular bumps) via ISTA + dictionary update, with or without penalty ||alpha(Tx) - A alpha(x)||^2; fit A by least squares; track noisy shifting sequences with a Kalman filter using A.
experiments.intervention: Toggle the MR penalty weight (0 vs 0.5).
experiments.control: Unpenalized dictionary; Kalman with identity transition.
experiments.observable: Permutation-likeness PL = mean over rows of max|A_ij| / sum_j|A_ij|; cyclic residual ||A^32 - I||_F / ||I||_F; tracking MSE ratio vs identity-transition Kalman.
experiments.success_criterion: Over 10 seeds: mean penalized PL >= 0.80 AND unpenalized PL <= 0.50 AND penalized tracking MSE <= 0.70 x identity-transition MSE AND null-twin PL <= 0.40.
experiments.failure_criterion: Penalized PL < 0.60, or penalized minus unpenalized PL < 0.15, or tracking MSE ratio > 0.90.
experiments.alternative_explanation: The penalty merely makes the dictionary convolutional/shift-tied, a known construction.
experiments.null_twin: Train with pairs (x, x') where x' is a random other sample: same marginals, no transform relation.
experiments.why_this_implementation: Small dense tensors are the natural substrate for dictionary learning; sparse inference is ISTA (an optimizer, not a neural network) and the transition is a linear map.
stupid_explanations: penalty shrinks codes onto few atoms so A becomes diagonal-dominant and PL is trivially high
the signal generator is itself shift-tied, so any dictionary learns shifted bumps
tracking gain comes from better denoising, not from the transition

experiments.hypothesis: A warm-started sparse tracker has a self-sealing region (stale support while the support MR passes) whose boundary is set by the single combined variable K/lambda.
experiments.mechanism: Latent 3-of-32 support switching with probability 0.02/step, known dictionary, noisy 16-dim observations; LCA inference initialized from a Kalman prediction with gain K; support MR = support identity under independent re-noising of the observation.
experiments.intervention: Sweep 8 K values x 8 lambda values.
experiments.control: Cold-start LCA over the same grid.
experiments.positive_control: Force K = 0 (pure prediction) in 4 extra cells: these must be self-sealing.
experiments.observable: Per cell: switch detection latency, MR violation rate, self-sealing indicator (latency > 50 steps AND violation rate < 0.01).
experiments.success_criterion: At least 5 of 64 cells self-sealing AND logistic regression of the indicator on log(K/lambda) alone has AUC >= 0.90 AND adding log K and log lambda separately reduces deviance by < 10% AND null twin has <= 1 self-sealing cell.
experiments.failure_criterion: Fewer than 3 self-sealing cells, or AUC(log K/lambda) < 0.75, or null twin has at least as many self-sealing cells as the warm-started tracker.
experiments.alternative_explanation: Generic hysteresis of any thresholded tracker with momentum; nothing specific to the three concepts.
experiments.null_twin: Cold-start tracker plus an exponential moving average on codes with equal effective memory: Kalman gain structure removed, smoothing and noise matched.
experiments.why_this_implementation: A small iterative optimizer (LCA) captures thresholded competition directly; no network training needed.
stupid_explanations: latency threshold chosen so a region trivially exists
re-noising amplitude too small to ever flip support, so the MR always passes
K and lambda correlated in the grid design

experiments.hypothesis: When MR residuals reveal only the projection of a fault outside the relation kernel, a sparse fault prior recovers the full fault including its kernel component, while min-norm recovery cannot.
experiments.mechanism: Mirror filters on x and T x over a 20-dim linear system; faults are biases in a 40-atom sensor-fault dictionary; accumulated whitened MR residual y = P f + noise; recover f by Lasso vs min-norm least squares.
experiments.positive_control: Faults placed entirely outside the kernel (both methods should recover).
experiments.observable: Relative recovery error ||f_hat - f|| / ||f||; recovered kernel-energy fraction.
experiments.success_criterion: For k <= 3 over 200 trials: Lasso error <= 0.20 in >= 80% of trials AND min-norm error >= 0.50 in >= 80% of trials AND null-twin Lasso error <= 0.20 in <= 20% of trials.
experiments.failure_criterion: Lasso success < 50% at k <= 3, or null-twin success rate within 15 percentage points of the sparse case.
experiments.alternative_explanation: This is ordinary compressed sensing; the MR and filter are incidental.
experiments.null_twin: Dense faults (Gaussian over all 40 atoms) with the same total energy and the same kernel-energy fraction.
experiments.why_this_implementation: A linear-algebraic causal toy: the relation kernel and projection are exact, so outcomes are decidable; Lasso and linear filters only, no learning ontology.
stupid_explanations: projection rank high enough that no recovery is needed
Lasso lambda tuned on the test trials
an incoherent fault dictionary makes any method work
procedural_notes: 'k <= 3' read as every k before the run; pooled reading would have been SIGNAL (0.823)

anomalies.text: Spec positive control (row(P) faults, 'both methods recover') cannot satisfy the min-norm >= 0.50 clause by construction; pilot attempt 1 failed on it and was repaired (pre-declared) to oracle-support LS on the sparse faults.
